lines.text: $BCF'B'$ is a parallelogram ($BB' \parallel CF'$ and $B'F' \parallel BC$ by construction), so $|B'F'|=|BC|$ (opposite sides of a parallelogram).
$|BC|=|AB|$ (given), so $|B'F'|=|AB|$.
$|\angle BAE'|=|\angle E'F'B'|$ (alternate angles, $AB \parallel F'B'$).
$|\angle AE'B|=|\angle F'E'B'|$ (vertically opposite angles).
$\triangle ABE'$ and $\triangle F'B'E'$ are congruent (ASA), so $|AE'|=|F'E'|$.
$|AE'|=|DE|$ and $|F'E'|=|FE|$ (opposite sides of parallelograms $ADEE'$ and $E'EFF'$).
Therefore $|DE|=|EF|$.

steps.title: Step A: write the Given and the To Prove

lines.text: Draw $\triangle ABC$ and the smaller similar triangle $\triangle A'B'C'$.
Given: $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle A'B'C'$ are similar, so their angles are equal: $|\angle A| = |\angle A'|$, $|\angle B| = |\angle B'|$, $|\angle C| = |\angle C'|$.
To prove: $\dfrac{|AB|}{|A'B'|} = \dfrac{|BC|}{|B'C'|} = \dfrac{|CA|}{|C'A'|}$.

steps.title: Step B: construct a copy of A'B'C' inside ABC

lines.text: Mark $B''$ on $[AB]$ so that $|AB''| = |A'B'|$.
Mark $C''$ on $[AC]$ so that $|AC''| = |A'C'|$.
Join $B''$ to $C''$.

steps.title: Step C: show the copy is congruent to A'B'C'

lines.text: $|AB''| = |A'B'|$ (construction), $|\angle A| = |\angle A'|$ (given), $|AC''| = |A'C'|$ (construction).
So $\triangle AB''C''$ is congruent to $\triangle A'B'C'$. Reason: SAS.

steps.title: Step D: show B''C'' is parallel to BC

lines.text: By congruence, $|\angle AB''C''| = |\angle A'B'C'| = |\angle ABC|$.
These are corresponding angles, so $B''C'' \parallel BC$. Reason: corresponding angles are equal.

steps.title: Step E: use the parallel line to get the ratios

lines.text: A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio, so $\dfrac{|AB|}{|AB''|} = \dfrac{|AC|}{|AC''|}$.
Replace $|AB''|$ by $|A'B'|$ and $|AC''|$ by $|A'C'|$ (construction): $\dfrac{|AB|}{|A'B'|} = \dfrac{|AC|}{|A'C'|}$.
Repeat the argument starting from vertex $B$ (mark points on $[BA]$ and $[BC]$): $\dfrac{|AB|}{|A'B'|} = \dfrac{|BC|}{|B'C'|}$.
Hence $\dfrac{|AB|}{|A'B'|} = \dfrac{|BC|}{|B'C'|} = \dfrac{|CA|}{|C'A'|}$.
